accepted.name: projects_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id,
  acronym,
  title,
  ec_call,
  ec_fund_scheme,
  cordis_ref,
  ec_ref,
  start_date,
  end_date,
  start_year,
  end_year,
  homepage,
  total_cost,
  ec_max_contribution,
  framework_program,
  objective,
  principal_investigator
FROM projects
accepted.description: Normalized/cleaned projection of the projects table exposing key identifiers, descriptive attributes, and core measures. Use this as the canonical projects relation for joins, year-based aggregations, and timeline analyses. | Use for: Time-series of projects per start_year or end_year; Budget aggregations (total_cost, ec_max_contribution) by programme/fund scheme; Joining projects to participants or dimensions (institutions, countries, topics)

accepted.name: project_members_clean
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id,
  project,
  pic_number,
  rcn,
  member_name,
  activity_type,
  country,
  street,
  city,
  postal_code,
  ec_contribution,
  institution_id,
  member_role,
  geocode_regions_3,
  member_short_name,
  department_name,
  vat_number,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  region_code,
  region_name
FROM project_members
accepted.description: Cleaned projection of project_members exposing participant-level financials, location, and role. Keeps identifiers needed for joins to projects and institutions. | Use for: Aggregate participant contributions per project or country; Map participant institutions to regions and compute regional participation; Filter members by member_role or activity_type

accepted.name: projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  p.acronym AS acronym,
  p.title AS title,
  pp.programme AS programme,
  psa.subject_area AS subject_area,
  pt.topic AS topic
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN project_programmes pp ON pp.project = p.unics_id
LEFT JOIN project_subject_areas psa ON psa.project = p.unics_id
LEFT JOIN project_topics pt ON pt.project = p.unics_id
accepted.description: Denormalized view joining projects to their programmes, subject areas, and topics. One row per project-per-linked-value for each bridge; useful for filtering or grouping by programme/subject/topic. Preserve keys to enable downstream aggregation or de-duplication. | Use for: Count projects per programme/subject/topic; Find projects associated with a combination of programme and subject area; Filter projects by topic

accepted.name: project_financials_by_member
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.project AS project,
  pm.unics_id AS unics_id,
  SUM(pm.ec_contribution) AS total_ec_contribution_by_member,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY pm.project) AS member_count_in_project
FROM project_members pm
GROUP BY pm.project, pm.unics_id
accepted.description: Aggregated financial measures at the project-member and project level: sum of ec_contribution per project and per project-member, plus member counts per project. Useful for budget breakdowns and per-member contribution analysis. | Use for: Total participant EC contribution per project; Share of project budget per participant (join to projects_core.total_cost); Projects with many participants

accepted.name: projects_yearly_budget_rollup
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  start_year,
  framework_program,
  COUNT(unics_id) AS projects_count,
  SUM(total_cost) AS total_cost_sum,
  SUM(ec_max_contribution) AS ec_max_contribution_sum
FROM projects
GROUP BY start_year, framework_program
accepted.description: Year-level aggregation of projects financials by start_year and framework_program. Produces counts and sums per year+framework suitable for trend analysis. Keeps framework_program for joins to ec_framework_programs. | Use for: Budget trends by year and framework program; Compare total_cost vs ec_max_contribution over time; Identify years with most projects per framework

accepted.name: projects_principal_investigators
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  p.acronym AS acronym,
  p.title AS title,
  p.principal_investigator AS principal_investigator,
  pe.full_name AS principal_investigator_name
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN people pe ON pe.unics_id = p.principal_investigator
accepted.description: Projects joined to the people table to expose principal investigator names alongside project identifiers. Useful for contacting PIs or listing PI-led projects. | Use for: List projects with PI names; Find PI workload (count projects per PI); Contact PIs for a set of projects

accepted.name: institution_locations
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.unics_id AS unics_id,
  i.institutions_name AS institutions_name,
  i.country_id AS country_id,
  c.country_name AS country_name,
  c.country_code2 AS country_code2,
  c.country_code3 AS country_code3,
  i.geocode_regions_3 AS geocode_regions_3,
  i.acronym AS acronym,
  i.short_name AS short_name,
  i.website AS website
FROM institutions i
LEFT JOIN countries c ON c.unics_id = i.country_id
accepted.description: Institutions with country and region codes preserved for geospatial or regional analysis. Joins institutions to countries to expose country_name and codes. Useful for mapping institutions or grouping by country. | Use for: Count projects or members by institution country; Map institution distribution by region; Join institution data to project_members.institution_id

accepted.name: projects_rank_by_total_cost
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id,
  acronym,
  title,
  start_year,
  total_cost,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY start_year ORDER BY total_cost DESC) AS total_cost_rank_within_year
FROM projects
accepted.description: Rank projects by total_cost within each start_year. Exposes a rank column so callers can filter downstream (e.g., top-k per year) without embedding literals here. | Use for: Select top-k most expensive projects per year (WHERE total_cost_rank_within_year <= K); Analyze distribution of project budgets within years

accepted.name: project_member_counts_by_country
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.project AS project,
  pm.country AS country,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pm.unics_id) AS distinct_member_count,
  SUM(pm.ec_contribution) AS total_ec_contribution_by_country
FROM project_members pm
GROUP BY pm.project, pm.country
accepted.description: Counts of distinct project members and sum of EC contributions grouped by project and member country. Useful for evaluating country-level participation in each project. | Use for: Which countries contributed most to a given project; Aggregate member counts by country across projects; Map financing by country within projects

accepted.name: erc_panel_assignments
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  p.acronym AS acronym,
  pep.panel AS panel,
  ep.description AS panel_description,
  ep.part_of AS panel_part_of
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN project_erc_panels pep ON pep.project = p.unics_id
LEFT JOIN erc_panels ep ON ep.code = pep.panel
accepted.description: Projects joined with their ERC panel code and panel description. Preserves project id and panel code for filtering and grouping by panel. | Use for: List projects by ERC panel; Aggregate budgets by ERC panel; Filter projects to a panel or panel group (panel_part_of)
